chapterNote: The darkest psalm in the Psalter, and the only one that never turns toward the light. Heman the Ezrahite — traditionally both one of Solomon's proverbial wise men and a chief temple singer — has been sick since his youth, counted among the dead, set loose among them like the slain God no longer remembers, shut up where his friends cannot bear to look at him. Every affliction is God's doing and he says so: You have set me down in the lowest pit; Your wrath presses hard on me; with all Your breakers You have brought me low; You have made me a thing they cannot stand to look at. The middle of the psalm is its one argument, the one Hezekiah also used: the dead do not praise You — will Your covenant love be recounted in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon, Your righteousness in the land of forgetting? The questions expect no; the resurrection is the answer he could not yet give. The last Hebrew word is 'darkness.' The church has kept the psalm exactly there — Good Friday, the deathbed — because some nights do not end before morning and the faithful need words for them. But the first line is 'O LORD, God of my salvation,' and every verse after it is still addressed to Him: the psalm's whole instruction is that a man can keep spreading his palms toward the top of the pit.

1.text: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choir director, according to Mahalath Leannoth. A contemplation of Heman the Ezrahite. O LORD, God of my salvation, by day I have cried out, and by night, before You.
1.amp: A Song [shir] or Psalm [mizmor] for the sons [ben] of Korah, to the chief Musician [natsach] upon Mahalath Leannoth [anah — to afflict], Maschil [maskil] of Heman the Ezrahite ['A Psalm of Heman the Ezrahite, giving instruction', maskil, the KJV margin]. O LORD [YHWH] God [Elohim] of my salvation [yeshuah], I have cried [tsaaq] day [yom] and night [layil] before You:
1.notes: YHWH Elohe yeshuati (H3068, H430, H3444): 'LORD, God of my salvation' — the one line of confession in the darkest psalm in the Psalter, and it comes first; yom-tsaaqti ba-lailah negdekha (H3117, H6817, H3915): by day I have cried out, in the night, before You. Heman the Ezrahite (H1968, H250) is traditionally identified both with one of Solomon's proverbial wise men (1 Kings 4:31) and with the chief temple singer of that name (1 Chronicles 6:33), though the genealogies place them in different tribes; Mahalath Leannoth (H4257, H6031) is probably a tune name, 'sickness, for afflicting' — fitting. Maskil: a teaching psalm; what it teaches is how to keep praying in the dark.

2.text: Let my prayer come into Your presence; bend Your ear to my ringing cry.
2.amp: Let my prayer [tephillah] come [bo] before [panim] You: incline [natah] Your ear [ozen] unto my cry [rinnah — ringing cry];
2.notes: tabo le-phanekha tephillati (H935, H6440, H8605): let my prayer COME before Your face — the doubt is whether it will arrive; hatteh-oznekha le-rinnati (H5186, H241, H7440): tilt Your ear to my rinnah, the ringing cry that elsewhere is joy (Psalm 126:2) and here is not. The only requests the psalm makes: be heard.

3.text: For my soul is full to the brim with troubles, and my life has reached the edge of Sheol.
3.amp: For my soul [nephesh] is full [saba — sated] of troubles [ra — evils]: and my life [chay] draws nigh [naga — touches] unto the grave [sheol].
3.notes: ki-sabeah be-raot naphshi (H7646, H7451, H5315): my soul is SATED with evils — saba, the full-stomach word of Psalm 104:28, grimly inverted; ve-chayyai li-sheol higgiu (H2416, H7585, H5060): and my life has TOUCHED Sheol. Not near: touching.

4.text: I am counted among those going down to the pit; I am like a strong man with no strength left,
4.amp: I am counted [chashab — reckoned] with them that go down [yarad] into the pit [bor]: I am as a man [geber — strong man] that has no strength [eyal]:
4.notes: nechshabti im-yorde bor (H2803, H3381, H953): I am RECKONED with the pit-descenders — already on their list; hayiti ke-geber en-eyal (H1397, H353): I have become like a geber — a man in his strength — with no eyal, no vigor: the word for a warrior applied to someone who cannot lift his head.

5.text: set loose among the dead, like the slain lying in the grave, whom You remember no more, and they are cut off from Your hand.
5.amp: Free [chophshi — released] among the dead [muth], like the slain [chalal — pierced] that lie [shakab] in the grave, whom You remember [zakar] no more: and they are cut off [gazar] from ['by', yad, the KJV margin] Your hand.
5.notes: ba-metim chophshi (H4191, H2670): 'free among the dead' — chophshi, the word for a slave set free (Exodus 21:2), here the terrible freedom of being discharged from the living. kemo chalalim shokhebe qeber (H2491, H7901): like the pierced who lie in the grave — asher lo zekhartam od (H2142): whom You remember no more — ve-hemmah mi-yadekha nigzaru (H3027, H1504): and they are cut off from Your hand — or, the margin, 'by' it. The dead as the one class God has stopped remembering: the psalm's theology is Old Testament Sheol at its bleakest, before Easter.

6.text: You have set me down in the lowest pit, in the dark places, down in the deeps.
6.amp: You have laid [shith] me in the lowest [tachti] pit [bor], in darkness [machshakim — dark places], in the deeps.
6.notes: shattani be-bor tachtiyyot (H7896, H953, H8482): You have SET me in the pit of the lowest places — the same word as Psalm 63:9 and 86:13; be-machashakkim bi-metsolot (H4285): in dark places, in the deeps — the ocean floor of Jonah 2:3. And the subject of the verb is 'You': the psalm never blames anyone else.

7.text: Your wrath presses hard on me, and with all Your breakers You have brought me low. Selah.
7.amp: Your wrath [chemah — hot fury] lies hard [samak — presses down] upon me, and You have afflicted [anah — brought low] me with all Your waves [mishbar — breakers]. Selah [Selah].
7.notes: alai samekhah chamatekha (H5564, H2534): on me Your fury LEANS — samak, the priest's hand pressed on the sacrifice's head (Leviticus 1:4): the psalmist as the animal under the hand. ve-khol-mishbarekha innita (H4867, H6031): and with all Your breakers You have humbled me — Psalm 42:7's 'all Your waves and Your billows', with the title's word innita, 'for afflicting'. Selah, in the middle of a drowning.

8.text: You have put those who know me far from me; You have made me a thing they cannot stand to look at; I am shut in and cannot get out.
8.amp: You have put away [rachaq — distanced] mine acquaintance [yada] far [rachaq] from me; You have made [shith] me an abomination [toebah] unto them: I am shut up [kala — confined], and I cannot come forth [yatsa].
8.notes: hirchaqta meyuddaai mimmenni (H7368, H3045): You have DISTANCED my acquaintances from me — shattani toebot lamo (H7896, H8441): made me toebot, abominations, to them — the plural: a whole category of disgust, a leper's word — kalu ve-lo etse (H3607, H3318): shut in, and I cannot get out. Job 19:13-19 and the leper outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46) in one verse; the isolation is presented as God's doing, like everything else here.

9.text: My eye wastes away from affliction; I have called on You, LORD, every day; I have spread out my palms to You.
9.amp: Mine eye [ayin] mourns [daab — pines away] by reason of affliction [oni]: LORD [YHWH], I have called [qara] daily [yom] upon You, I have stretched out my hands [kaph — palms] unto You.
9.notes: eni daabah minni-oni (H5869, H1669, H6040): my eye pines from affliction — the same wasting eye as Psalm 6:7 and 31:9, though those use a different verb, ashesh; qeratikha YHWH be-khol-yom (H7121, H3068, H3117): I have called You every day — shittachti elekha khappai (H3709): I have spread my palms to You. The middle of the psalm and its one act: the man in the pit keeps his hands open toward the top of it.

10.text: Will You work a wonder for the dead? Will the shades rise up and thank You? Selah.
10.amp: Will You show [asah] wonders [pele] to the dead [muth]? shall the dead [repaim — the shades] arise [qum] and praise [yadah — thank] You? Selah [Selah].
10.notes: ha-la-metim taaseh-pele (H4191, H6213, H6382): for the dead will You do a WONDER? — im-rephaim yaqumu yodukha (H7496, H6965, H3034): will the repaim, the shades, the weak ones of the underworld (Isaiah 14:9), rise and thank You? Verses 10-12 are the psalm's argument — the one Hezekiah also used (Isaiah 38:18-19): keep me alive because the dead do not sing. Every question expects 'no'; the resurrection is the answer the psalmist could not yet give.

11.text: Will Your covenant love be recounted in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon?
11.amp: Shall Your lovingkindness [chesed — covenant love] be declared [saphar — recounted] in the grave? or Your faithfulness [emunah] in destruction [Abaddon — the place of perishing]?
11.notes: ha-yesuppar ba-qeber chasdekha (H5608, H2617): will Your chesed be recounted in the grave — emunatekha ba-abaddon (H530, H11): Your faithfulness in Abaddon, 'Perishing', the underworld's name in Job 26:6 and Proverbs 15:11, and the name of the angel of the pit in Revelation 9:11. Chesed, the first covenant word of Exodus 34:6, and emunah, sister-word of that verse's emet — both from aman, to be firm — asked whether they have any hearing down there.

12.text: Will Your wonder be known in the darkness, or Your righteousness in the land of forgetting?
12.amp: Shall Your wonders [pele] be known [yada] in the dark [choshek]? and Your righteousness [tsedaqah] in the land [eretz] of forgetfulness?
12.notes: ha-yivvada ba-choshekh pilekha (H3045, H2822, H6382): will Your wonder be KNOWN in the dark — ve-tsidqatekha be-erets neshiyyah (H6666, H776): and Your righteousness in the land of neshiyyah, forgetting — a word used only here: the country where nothing is remembered, the opposite of verse 5's God who remembers no more. Sheol as mutual amnesia.

13.text: But as for me — to You, LORD, I have cried for help, and in the morning my prayer comes to meet You.
13.amp: But unto You have I cried [shava — shouted for help], O LORD [YHWH]; and in the morning [boqer] shall my prayer [tephillah] prevent [qadam — come before, meet] You.
13.notes: va-ani elekha YHWH shivvati (H3068, H7768): 'and I' — to You, LORD, I have SHOUTED — u-ba-boqer tephillati teqaddemekka (H1242, H8605, H6923): and in the morning my prayer goes out to MEET You, qadam, the old sense of 'prevent': it is at the door before dawn. Psalm 5:3's morning prayer, with no expectation stated — only the habit kept.

14.text: Why, LORD, do You cast off my soul? Why do You hide Your face from me?
14.amp: LORD [YHWH], why do You cast off [zanach — reject] my soul [nephesh]? why do You hide [satar] Your face [panim] from me?
14.notes: lamah YHWH tiznach naphshi (H3068, H2186, H5315): why, LORD, do You REJECT my soul — zanach, Psalm 43:2's and 44:9's verb; tastir panekha mimmenni (H5641, H6440): why hide Your face from me. Two whys and no answer: the psalm asks the question Job asked and gets Job's silence.

15.text: I have been afflicted and close to death from my youth; I have carried Your terrors; I am distraught.
15.amp: I am afflicted [ani] and ready to die [gava — expiring] from my youth [noar] up: while I suffer [nasa — carry] Your terrors [emah] I am distracted.
15.notes: ani ani ve-goea minnoar (H6041, H1478, H5290): afflicted I am, and expiring, from youth — a lifelong sickness, not a bad month; nasati emekha aphunah (H5375, H367): I have CARRIED Your terrors — I am aphunah, a word used only here: numb, distraught, gone dark inside. The psalm's sufferer is not a man having a crisis; he is a man whose whole life has been one.

16.text: Your burning anger has swept over me; Your terrors have destroyed me.
16.amp: Your fierce wrath [charon — burning anger] goes over [abar — passes over] me; Your terrors [biuthim — alarms] have cut me off.
16.notes: alai aberu charonekha (H5674, H2740): over me Your burnings have PASSED — abar, the verb for the LORD passing through Egypt to smite (Exodus 12:12, 23) — the passing over of the door is a different verb, pasach — and no lamb's blood on this door; biutekha tsimmetutuni (H1161): Your terrors have annihilated me — biuthim, Job's word for God's frights (Job 6:4). Every noun of wrath in the psalm is 'Your'.

17.text: They surround me like water all day long; they have closed in on me all together.
17.amp: They came round about [sabab] me daily ['all the day', yom, the KJV margin] like water [mayim]; they compassed me about together [yachad].
17.notes: sabbuni kha-mayim kol-ha-yom (H5437, H4325, H3117): they surround me like water 'all the day', the margin's literal — the terrors, or the waves of verse 7, rising to the chin; hiqqiphu alai yachad (H3162): they have closed the ring on me together. Jonah 2:5's waters, without Jonah's fish.

18.text: You have put lover and friend far from me; those who know me — darkness.
18.amp: Lover [ahab] and friend [rea] have You put far [rachaq] from me, and mine acquaintance [yada] into darkness [machshakim].
18.notes: hirchaqta mimmenni oheb va-rea (H7368, H157, H7453): You have distanced from me lover and friend — verse 8 again, tighter; meyuddaai machshakh (H3045, H4285): my acquaintances — darkness. The Hebrew ends on that one word, machshakh, and the psalm ends with it: no turn, no vow, no praise, the only psalm in the Psalter to close in the dark. The church has kept it there on purpose — read on Good Friday, prayed by the dying — because some nights do not end before morning, and this psalm gives them words. And it is still addressed, every line of it, to 'the God of my salvation' (v. 1).
